theory_content: Central bank rate changes influence borrowing costs, valuations, and investor appetite for risk. Higher rates often pressure growth valuations and slow credit-sensitive sectors.
Inflation measures how quickly prices rise across the economy. Moderate inflation can support growth, but high inflation can reduce real returns and force tighter monetary policy.
Economies move through expansion, peak, contraction, and recovery phases. Different sectors often outperform at different points in the cycle.
